historical_theory_findings.title: Label-shift radius is not a symmetric identified interval
historical_theory_findings.explanation: The affine image of a simplex fibre need not equal [Delta-rho,Delta+rho] when rho is the largest absolute displacement from the current truth. A fibre with attainable benefit [1/5,3/5], truth Delta=1/5 and rho=2/5 is uniformly positive despite |Delta|<rho. Thus the stated iff and opposite-sign necessity fail.
historical_theory_findings.treatment: Replace with actual lower/upper benefit extrema before promotion. Retain the valid evidence-monotonicity result at lines 47-54. This historical failure is separate from the newer MVC track.

historical_theory_findings.title: Repaired computability construction still puts a noncomputable real into the input law
historical_theory_findings.explanation: For computable o and nonzero computable m0, Q_o=(1-m0)Unif[-1,1]+m0 delta_(o-s) has bounded continuous first moment m0(o-s), revealing the noncomputable Specker s. The claimed modulus s-s_lower(t) is not computable. The validator instead uses a finite perfect-square toy set and a known tail, so its success does not establish computability for a halting-set construction.
historical_theory_findings.treatment: Withdraw CLOSED as a proved characterization until a correct construction and computable-analysis argument exist; retain numerical bisection examples only as examples.

historical_theory_findings.title: A binary-margin counterexample does not refute every scalar capacity
historical_theory_findings.explanation: The theorem asserts failure for every proposed scalar K and worlds with K(O)>beta, but does not rule out a conservative K identically zero. Multiple components in mu also do not imply a threshold on an arbitrary nonmonotone scalar O(mu) identifies at most one component. The proof establishes that the selected binary margin is insufficient, not that all scalar functionals fail.
historical_theory_findings.treatment: Narrow to the concrete reduct failure; require an explicit admissible statistic family and nontrivial power criterion for any universal impossibility.

historical_theory_findings.title: Weakest-class counterexample leaves the probability model
historical_theory_findings.explanation: a=2 eta_a-1 must lie in [-1,1], but the proposed witness uses a2=+/-2 and benefit +3/2. The later canonical-class proof also treats global swap closure as if it implied independently free regional signs, an additional condition not implied by a global involution.
historical_theory_findings.treatment: Do not promote the weakest-class characterization or simulation counts as proofs. Preserve as an explicitly failed historical attempt.

historical_theory_findings.title: One representative per swap orbit need not orient an evidence fibre
historical_theory_findings.explanation: The formal four-world construction has two swap orbits, identical evidence, and opposite selected benefits. It refutes orbit-selection sufficiency. The replacement bool_decoder_iff_constant_on_fibres is set-theoretic, not a measurable-selection theorem.
historical_theory_findings.treatment: Keep the counterexample and correct fibre-consistency condition visible; preserve valid measurable-swap necessity, not false one-bit sufficiency. Already honestly disclosed in active supplement.

historical_theory_findings.title: Disagreement-conditioned H degenerates the focal binary pair
historical_theory_findings.explanation: On D, focal binary correctness indicators C0 and Ca are complementary. Conditional independence forces them deterministic given Y; per-class symmetric accuracy then makes the focal accuracies 0/1. Thus the proposed nondegenerate H/ratio-rate model needs a separate consistent construction. The rank-one proof also uses pi(1-pi)>0 without declaring that assumption.
historical_theory_findings.treatment: Keep historical H/ratio-rate results outside paper until corrected model and rates are justified.

historical_theory_findings.title: Two-sided miscoverage delta does not give a delta/2 one-sided bound
historical_theory_findings.explanation: The parenthesis 'in fact delta/2' requires an equal-tail/symmetry condition. All delta miscoverage can occur in one tail. The subsequent Bonferroni argument still works at delta under its actual coverage premise.
historical_theory_findings.treatment: Retain corrected fixed-candidate family-wise composition as useful conditional theory; remove unsupported halving.

The numerical validator mixes these conventions.

do_not_promote_unqualified: Main 203–208 states a STRICT variance improvement from calibration without Var(s)>0. Constant calibrated score s=1/2 gives equality, so the correct general relation is <=.

Main 227–229 gives an exact break-even expression, while proof 95–96 uses asymptotic label counts and ignores the linear Bernstein term and integer rounding. Present it as a scaling comparison, not an exact operational price.

Weighted-conformal exactness in main 253–259 requires the true ratio (plus correct weighted score protocol); learning an estimated ratio does not inherit exact finite-sample coverage automatically.

additional_research_with_qualifications.family: Labeled, transport, and witness-class audited budgets
additional_research_with_qualifications.safe_core: Direct labeled Hoeffding audit and transport/IPM transfer are useful given iid labels, fixed predictors, a COMMON residual u across calibration/target, and the declared regularity/witness-class containment. Input transport alone cannot bound target concept drift.
additional_research_with_qualifications.proof_cautions: Aud-H proof 235–237 assigns range 2L/n to each bounded difference but its stated McDiarmid term is too small for that calculation: the direct theorem gives L*sqrt(2 log(1/delta)/n), not L*sqrt(log(1/delta)/(2n)). Even the displayed statement 209–210 is smaller than that direct derivation. This is a proof/constants gap, not a separately established counterexample to every conceivable sharper argument. Its root-n usefulness conclusion also needs labeled and deployment sample sizes to scale, and computable IPM/complexity bounds if called an algorithm. Aud-B's strict power condition should not silently turn > into >= at its sample-size boundary.
additional_research_with_qualifications.already_active: body 492–498 ALREADY describes target labels and structural coupling. The label-free audit impossibility itself has a stronger current fibre-wise statement at body 429–457. Do not call that negative ingredient missing.

additional_research_with_qualifications.family: Regression noise cancellation and bounded-drift bracket
additional_research_with_qualifications.safe_core: For finite squared risks and integrable terms, conditional mean-zero noise cancels from expected paired squared-loss difference. Full measurable bounded drift gives exact interval [U-2T_S-2BW,U-2T_S+2BW], achieved by signed extremal drifts; strict sign is identifiable exactly when this interval excludes zero.
additional_research_with_qualifications.cautions: Arbitrary mean-zero noise can have infinite variance, making R(f0)-R(fa)=infinity-infinity undefined. W>0 is needed for the displayed B-star ratio. If B=W=U-2T_S=0, ternary sign 0 is identifiable although the claimed strict > iff fails; use strict-direction semantics. In proof 59–60 the absolute-value Holder equality is not iff b=-B sign(f0-fa): the positive signed extremizer also attains absolute equality. Finite-sample U,W are not known exactly from finite unlabeled data unless separately assumed or bounded.
additional_research_with_qualifications.already_active: No substantive regression theorem found in the 23-source live closure. This is a genuinely absent scoped extension, not already implied by the binary frontier or a scalar Lean reflexivity identity.
